---
title: "Historical maps"
---

The ice sheets drawn as old charts, from the same data as the posters: ice flow
in rust to oxblood over the hillshaded surface, water lining along the coasts,
waves on the sea beyond the median winter sea-ice edge and floes inside it. On
them are the routes of historical expeditions and where penguins breed and
Arctic animals gather. The Greenland map uses Greenlandic (kalaallisut) names
and terms: *Kalaallit Nunaat* is Greenland, "the land of the Greenlanders", and
*Sermersuaq* the ice sheet.

{{< include _gallery_vintage.md >}}

## Routes

The routes are transcribed from the expedition accounts and published
positions; every point and its source are listed in
[`data/routes_antarctica.csv`](https://github.com/fesmc/cryosphere-maps/blob/main/data/routes_antarctica.csv)
and
[`data/routes_greenland.csv`](https://github.com/fesmc/cryosphere-maps/blob/main/data/routes_greenland.csv).

- **Along the route** (camp and noon positions): Amundsen 1911–12 (*The South
  Pole*; Lantz, 2022, for the plateau), Scott 1911–12 (*Scott's Last
  Expedition*; Debenham, 1923), Shackleton 1908–09 (*The Heart of the
  Antarctic*) and the drift of the *Endurance* and the boat journey to
  Elephant Island 1915–16 (*South*; Worsley's log). Some longitudes are inferred
  from the stated course, as noted in the files.
- **Documented places only**, joined by arcs to show that the route between
  them is simplified: Mawson 1912–13, Fuchs–Hillary 1957–58, and in Greenland
  Nansen 1888, Peary 1892, the Danmark Expedition 1906–08, Koch–Wegener
  1912–13, Wegener 1930–31, the British Arctic Air Route Expedition 1930–31
  and the Expéditions Polaires Françaises 1949–51.

## Wildlife

- Emperor penguin colonies in 2023 (Fretwell, 2024, UK Polar Data Centre,
  doi:[10.5285/fb0547e4-d2c1-4580-8c98-182f1da7d9ae](https://doi.org/10.5285/fb0547e4-d2c1-4580-8c98-182f1da7d9ae)).
- Adélie penguin colonies from MAPPPD (Humphries et al., 2017,
  [penguinmap.com](https://www.penguinmap.com)), grouped within 100 km.
- Greenland: polar bear denning, musk-ox calving, walrus haul-out and narwhal
  summer areas from the Areas Important to Wildlife (Greenland Institute of
  Natural Resources and DCE, Aarhus University), one sign per area, grouped
  within 100 km.
